metadata.title: ICILS 2023 Technical Report (Test development, survey operations software, sampling, weights, questionnaire development, and quality assurance)
metadata.venue: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICILS 2023 uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design (stratified PPS school sampling, within-school class sampling, and student/teacher selection within classes) and computes final sampling weights for eligible and participating students. The final student weight (TOTWGTS) is the product of school base weight (WGTFAC1), school non-response adjustment (WGTADJ1S), class base weight (WGTFAC2S), class non-response adjustment (WGTADJ2S), and student non-response adjustment (WGTADJ3S). Weights are explicitly required for all findings in ICILS reporting, and participation/non-response adjudication is handled via within-school participation thresholds (e.g., schools with <50% within-school response are treated as non-participants). Replicate weights are not described in the provided excerpt; variance estimation is referenced as using jackknife replication in a later chapter, so replicate-weight usage is not extractable here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a technical report describing ICILS 2023 test development, instrument preparation, sampling, weighting, and quality assurance procedures rather than estimating achievement models with PVs. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable because no student-level PV-based predictive or scaling results are presented in the provided text excerpt. Missing-data handling is not reported here because the excerpt focuses on operational and methodological standards (e.g., sampling exclusions, participation thresholds, and weight construction) rather than an analysis pipeline that imputes or deletes missing item responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: ICILS 2023 targets students in the grade representing eight years of schooling with mean age at testing at least 13.5 and not older than 17; most countries test grade 8 (Norway tests grade 9; Romania tests grade 8 at the beginning of the next school year). Sampling excludes very small schools and schools exclusively for special needs students, and may exclude schools with different language of instruction or non-mainstream curricula; within-sample exclusions are permitted for students with intellectual disabilities, functional disabilities preventing participation, and non-native language speakers unable to overcome the language barrier (typically <1 year of instruction). Participation for inclusion in final estimates requires within-school response thresholds: schools with <50% within-school response for students or teachers are treated as non-participants and discarded from the respective survey. Additionally, student participation is defined as responding to at least one task in the achievement test, and class participation is required (e.g., at least 50% of students in a class participate) for the school to be considered participating for student weights.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 technical report does not present an empirical machine-learning prediction study; instead, it documents how ICILS 2023 constructs and delivers its computer-based assessments and how it ensures data quality and comparability across countries. It describes the test development timeline, including migration to online delivery, field-trial scorer training, and item/module selection using field-trial item analysis and item equating with trend modules to maintain scale continuity across cycles. It details the complex sampling design (stratified PPS school sampling, within-school class sampling, and student/teacher selection) and the computation of final sampling weights for students, teachers, and schools, including non-response adjustments and participation thresholds. It also reports quality assurance procedures (international quality control monitors, national quality monitoring, and survey activities questionnaires) and provides operational statistics on administration deviations and technical problems. As a result, the report’s “results” are methodological and operational (e.g., participation rates, administration compliance), not achievement-model performance metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided excerpt is a technical documentation of ICILS 2023 procedures (test development, software architecture, sampling, weighting, questionnaire development, and quality assurance) rather than an empirical ML paper with a defined predictive target, model training, and performance metrics. Consequently, there is no student-level ML algorithm evaluation, no PV-based outcome modeling, and no distinct dependent variable for which predictive effects could be extracted. The absence of main findings and ML techniques is therefore due to the document type and the excerpt’s focus on assessment and survey operations rather than analytical modeling.
